content:
AI Mentor — Document Indexing Pipeline

Full document path: from upload to semantic search readiness

Internal processing
Gemini API
Celery / Infra
PostgreSQL / pgvector
MinIO S3
1
Document Upload
User uploads a file via REST API. The file is stored in MinIO (S3), a Document record is created in the DB with status pending, then a Celery task is dispatched.
API entry points
documents/router.py uploads/router.py products/router.py
Storage
File → MinIO S3
Key: documents/{id}/original.{ext}
Celery task
ingest_document_task.delay(doc.id)
Supported sources
File, Archive (ZIP), URL, Confluence, GitHub, Website
2
Celery Worker: Download from S3
Worker picks up the ingest_document task, downloads the file from S3 to a temp directory, detects the format and runs ingest_from_bytes().
Task file
celery_app.py lines 233–337
Worker config
concurrency: 4
Queues: celery monitoring
soft_time_limit: 45 min, retry: up to 2
Libraries
Celery 5.x Redis (broker) boto3 / MinIO SDK
Format detection
pipeline.py → detect_format()
By extension + file content
3
Conversion to Markdown
All formats are converted to a unified representation — Markdown. Each format has its own converter. The result is saved to S3 as converted.md.
Converters by format
PDF → pymupdf4llmSwagger/OpenAPI → custom parserPostman → custom parserProtobuf → custom parserWSDL → custom parserXML → custom parserMD/TXT → as-is
PDF converter (main)
pymupdf4llm — text layer
Gemini Vision API — image OCR
Gemini — language detection
Files
converters/pdf.py converters/swagger.py converters/postman.py converters/proto.py converters/wsdl.py
4
Parsing into Sections
Markdown is split into sections by H1–H6 headings. Each section gets a heading_path — a hierarchical path like "Chapter > Section > Subsection".
Parser
parsers/markdown.py → parse_markdown()
Regex on ^#{1-6}\s+, skips headings inside code blocks
Result
list[Section] — objects with fields:
heading_path heading_level content
5
Chunking
Sections are split into optimally sized chunks. Large sections are split, small ones are merged. Code blocks and tables are kept atomic (never split).
Chunking parameters
max_tokens: 512
min_tokens: 50
overlap_paragraphs: 2
Token estimation: words × 1.3
Algorithm
1. Split text into atomic blocks (paragraphs, code, tables)
2. If section > max_tokens → _split_text()
3. If section < min_tokens → _merge_small_chunks()
4. Add overlap (2 trailing paragraphs from previous chunk)
Result
list[ChunkData]: heading_path, content, token_count, parent_content
File
ingestion/chunker.py chunk_sections()
6
Metadata Extraction (Gemini Flash)
Each chunk is sent to Gemini 2.5 Flash for document type classification and structured entity extraction (endpoints, parameters, protocols, keywords).
Model
Gemini 2.5 Flash (via OpenAI-compatible API)
Extracted data
doc_type: api_reference, user_guide, configuration, changelog, troubleshooting...
entities: api_endpoints, config_params, error_codes, protocols, keywords
File
ingestion/metadata_extractor.py
Library
httpx → OpenAI-compatible endpoint
7
Text Enrichment & Cleaning
Before embedding, text is cleaned of Markdown artifacts and enriched: heading_path, document type and entities are added as a contextual prefix.
Cleaning (text_cleaner.py)
Removes: bold/italic markers, links (keeps text), images, HTML tags, inline code
Unicode normalization → NFKC
Enrichment (enrich_for_embedding)
Prefix: [heading_path]
+ [type: api_reference]
+ [entities: GET /api/v1/..., ONVIF, ...]
Limit: 500 tokens (truncated if exceeded)
8
Vectorization — Embedding (Gemini)
Enriched chunks are sent in batches to Gemini Embedding API. Each chunk becomes a numeric vector of dimension 1024. Vectors are L2-normalized.
Model
gemini-embedding-2-preview
Dimensions: 1024
API parameters
task_type: RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT (indexing)
task_type: RETRIEVAL_QUERY (search)
Batch: up to 100 texts per request
Post-processing
L2 normalization via numpy:
vector / ||vector||₂
Library
google-genai (google.genai.Client)
numpy — normalization
Retry: up to 5 attempts with exp. backoff
File
ingestion/embedder.py → embed_texts() embed_query()
9
Storage in PostgreSQL + pgvector
Chunks, their metadata and embeddings are written to the chunks table. The vector is stored in a vector(1024) column. The document transitions to status ready.
chunks table
id, document_id, chunk_index,
heading_path, heading_level,
content (original), content_clean,
parent_content, token_count,
embedding vector(1024),
doc_type, entities (JSONB)
HNSW index
HNSW + vector_cosine_ops
m = 16, ef_construction = 128
ef_search = 128 (per query)

Metric: cosine similarity
1 - (a <=> b)
Libraries
SQLAlchemy (async) pgvector-python PostgreSQL 16
Document update
status → ready, indexed_at → now()
total_chunks, total_tokens, embedding_model,
embedding_dims, timing metrics
Where Gemini Is Used
Gemini Vision
Image OCR in PDF + language detection
Stage 3google-genai
Gemini 2.5 Flash
doc_type classification + entity extraction
Stage 6httpx → OpenAI API
gemini-embedding-2-preview
Vector generation (1024D) for semantic search
Stage 8google-genai
Gemini 2.5 Pro
Chat responses based on retrieved chunks
Search (RAG)httpx → OpenAI API
Key Libraries
google-genai
Gemini Embedding API + Gemini Vision (OCR)
Stages 3, 8
pymupdf4llm
PDF → Markdown (text layer)
Stage 3
numpy
L2 normalization of embeddings
Stage 8
pgvector-python
Vector type for SQLAlchemy + HNSW index
Stage 9
SQLAlchemy (async)
ORM, PostgreSQL queries
Stage 9
Celery + Redis
Task queues, background processing
Stage 2
httpx
HTTP client for OpenAI-compatible API (Gemini Flash/Pro)
Stages 6, RAG
